artifacts.summary: Confirms the self-clobbering redeploy hazard mechanism via a synthetic bash harness, surveys the hazard class down to two genuine call sites (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh:843 and command-gate-out.sh:176), evaluates the three candidate fixes, and recommends generalizing deploy-headless.sh's own existing main()-wrap self-overwrite-protection pattern to both sites.

memory_candidates.content: bash reads a running script incrementally by byte offset (not fully into memory), so a script that overwrites itself in-place mid-execution (or is overwritten by a subprocess it spawns) resumes at a stale offset -- silent truncation or garbled parsing, depending on the byte-length delta. Deterministic fix: wrap the entire remaining executable body in a single function, defined in full before it runs, invoked as the file's last statement -- bash must fully parse a compound command before executing any of it, so the function's body is already in memory before the overwrite (triggered by code inside it) can occur. A PARTIAL wrap (stopping mid-file) does not work: control returns to flat top-level code that still resumes reading the rewritten file at a stale offset. Verified with a synthetic self-rewriting harness (3/3 protected runs correct vs. 5/5 unprotected runs silently truncated).

When surveying a hazard class from a `grep -rln <pattern>` starting list, classify each hit by whether it is a genuine invocation (actually executes the risky call from live code) vs. a mention (echo/remedy string, doc comment, or test fixture) before treating the whole list as the hazard set. In this codebase's deploy-headless.sh hazard survey, 13 of 15 starting-list files were mention-only; only 2 were genuine invocation sites, independently corroborated by an existing in-repo doc (regeneration-is-manual-only.md) that already enumerated 'the exact and only sanctioned automated call sites'.
